summary: Over a 14-day analysis period, glucose management showed a strong overall Time in Range (86.0%) and mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL. However, significant safety risks exist due to recurrent overnight hypoglycemia (TBR up to 18.5% at 01:00 local time) and late-afternoon/evening hypoglycemia (TBR up to 15.3% at 19:00). A primary driver is unannounced meal handling combined with weekly GLP-1 dosing: unlogged meals force AAPS UAM/SMB logic to issue heavy micro-bolus stacks during late-afternoon glucose surges, which then crash into high evening profile basals and low target settings.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data coverage is excellent at 98.7% over 14 days with only minor gaps. Device and loop status telemetry are complete. Zero meal carbohydrate entries were logged in Nightscout across the entire period.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries out of 4,046 expected; largest gap 65.0 minutes; 0 carb entries logged.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged carbohydrate entries prevents direct, isolated calculation of meal Carb Ratios.

analysis_steps.findings: Primary safety risk is recurrent hypoglycemia concentrated in two time windows: overnight (23:00-04:00, TBR 10.1%-18.5%) and late afternoon/dinner transition (18:00-19:00, TBR 11.9%-15.3%). Extreme lows down to 41 mg/dL were recorded.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local TBR: 18.5% at 01:00, 10.2% at 03:00, 11.9% at 18:00, 15.3% at 19:00. Glucose extremes down to 41.0 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unrecorded manual rescue carbs leave exact duration of severe hypoglycemic events unconfirmed.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates (0.6-0.7 U/h) and overnight glucose target (90 mg/dL) are overly aggressive, forcing frequent 0 U/h temp basal suspensions. Evening basal increases to 0.6-0.7 U/h between 18:00 and 20:00 directly coincide with the daily peak in hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile target 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00; profile basal 0.6 U/h at 00:00, 0.7 U/h at 05:00, 0.6 U/h at 18:00, 0.7 U/h at 19:00. Loop frequently enacts 0 U/h temp basals overnight.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Distinguishing pure fasting basal needs from late GLP-1 meal absorption tails.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile DIA of 10.0 hours creates long tail IOB calculations. Dynamic ISF (70% adjustment factor) lowers effective ISF from 56 mg/dL/U down to 27-37 mg/dL/U during post-meal spikes, accelerating automated micro-bolusing.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile DIA = 10.0 h; profile ISF = 56 mg/dL/U flat; loop logs variable_sens down to 27.8 mg/dL/U during high glucose events.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Indirect CR estimation due to unannounced meals.

analysis_steps.findings: With zero carb entries, UAM logic and SMBs handle all meal coverage. GLP-1 gastric delay causes afternoon glucose spikes (14:00-17:00, TAR 32.1%), triggering intense UAM micro-bolus stacking (IOB peaking at 4.7-5.9 U) that subsequently causes severe evening drops.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_always_enabled=true; uam_enabled=true; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min; loop logs IOB > 5.0 U following unannounced afternoon surges.

analysis_steps.findings: Max IOB safety cap is set to 25.0 U, which exceeds 125% of the user's total daily insulin requirement (~19.7 U/day). This ceiling provides no practical safety guardrail against IOB stacking during unannounced meals or sensor noise.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_iob_units = 25.0 U; max_basal_u_per_hour = 12.0 U/h; total daily insulin = 275.95 U over 14 days (19.7 U/day).

analysis_steps.findings: Lack of pre-meal boluses forces complete reliance on reactive automated delivery. GLP-1 gastric delay causes delayed post-prandial surges that peak 3-4 hours after eating, driving late micro-bolus stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly glucose local shows peak average at 16:00 (162.8 mg/dL) dropping to 105.4 mg/dL at 19:00; weekly GLP-1 1.25 mg notes in telemetry.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carbohydrate timing and gram amounts are unrecorded.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended meal absorption over 4-6 hours matches expected GLP-1 pharmacodynamics. Profile meal_max_absorption_hours (7.0 h) accommodates slow digestion, but unannounced meals prevent structured e-carb distribution.
analysis_steps.evidence: meal_max_absorption_hours = 7.0 h; prolonged high glucose deviations lasting 4-5 hours post-meal.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or extended bolus entries logged in treatments.

analysis_steps.findings: Synthesized optimization priority: First, eliminate overnight and evening hypoglycemia by raising nighttime targets, reducing nighttime/evening basal rates, and lowering max IOB limits. Second, transition from unannounced meal reliance to logging meal carbohydrates with preboluses.
analysis_steps.evidence: Integrated findings from steps 1-8 confirming overnight TBR (up to 18.5%) and evening TBR (up to 15.3%) as primary safety targets.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Requires user verification of revised profile settings one parameter group at a time.

strengths: High overall Time in Range (86.0%) with average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL over 14 days.
Excellent CGM data coverage (98.7%) with minimal data transmission gaps.
Active closed-loop automation effectively prevents severe daytime hyperglycemia.
issues: Recurrent overnight hypoglycemia (Time Below Range reaches 18.5% at 01:00 local time).
Recurrent late-afternoon/evening hypoglycemia (Time Below Range reaches 15.3% at 19:00 local time).
Unannounced meals cause excessive reactive SMB stacking (IOB up to 5.9 U) driven by Dynamic ISF.
Unusually high Max IOB ceiling (25.0 U) relative to Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U/day).

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to Reduce Hypoglycemia
recommendations.description: Increase target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00 to provide a wider safety cushion during overnight sleep hours.

recommendations.title: Reduce Overnight and Evening Basal Rates
recommendations.description: Lower overnight basal (00:00-05:00) from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h, and evening basal (18:00-20:00) from 0.6-0.7 U/h to 0.5 U/h to eliminate persistent low glucose troughs.

recommendations.title: Tighten Maximum IOB Safety Guardrail
recommendations.description: Reduce Max IOB setting from 25.0 U to 7.0 U to prevent extreme automated insulin stacking during unannounced meals or sensor noise.

profile_recommendation.rationale: High overnight Time Below Range (18.5% at 01:00) and frequent 0 U/h temp basals indicate that the current 90 mg/dL target and 0.6 U/h overnight basal provide an insufficient safety margin.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight CGM trends for 3 consecutive nights to confirm glucose stability near 100 mg/dL without automated suspended basals.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise overnight target (23:00-08:00) from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL and reduce overnight basal (00:00-05:00) from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h.

parameter_decisions.rationale: High overnight TBR (18.5% at 01:00) and continuous 0 U/h loop temp basals indicate excessive nighttime basal delivery.
Early morning glucose is stable with low TBR (1.3%-2.5% at 06:00-07:00).
Morning baseline glucose remains well within target range.
Daytime glucose rise is driven by unannounced meals, not basal deficiency.
Basal rate at 16:00 is appropriate; late afternoon highs are caused by delayed meal absorption.
Stepping up basal to 0.6 U/h at 18:00 coincides with peak evening hypoglycemia (11.9%-15.3% TBR at 18:00-19:00).
Stepping up basal to 0.7 U/h at 19:00 exacerbates post-meal IOB drops during the dinner transition.
No overnight meal entries logged; insufficient evidence to modify CR.
No early morning meal entries logged; retain setting until meal bolusing is established.
Unannounced meals prevent exact CR calculation; retain pending carbohydrate logging.
Unannounced meals prevent exact CR calculation; maintain baseline setting.
No late evening meal entries logged; retain setting.
Profile ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U; Dynamic ISF adjusts effective sensitivity appropriately during high glucose.
Overnight target of 90 mg/dL provides insufficient safety margin given 10.1%-18.5% overnight TBR.
Daytime target of 100 mg/dL is appropriate and safe.
Raising target at 23:00 creates a safer transition into nighttime sleep.
10-hour DIA is configured in AAPS oref1; changing DIA alongside basal and target adjustments is not recommended.
SMB and UAM are necessary for closed-loop operation; unannounced meal management requires these enabled.
Activation conditions are appropriate for current unannounced meal usage.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery parameters are standard; safety capping should be handled via Max IOB rather than reduced SMB delivery timing.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current Max IOB (25 U) is over 125% of Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U/day). Lowering Max IOB to 7.0 U provides essential safety against stacking.
Dynamic ISF settings are functioning as intended; primary fixes must focus on target and basal rates first.
7-hour absorption model appropriately accommodates GLP-1 induced gastric slowing.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Log meal carbohydrates in AAPS, administer a 50% upfront meal bolus 10-15 minutes prior to eating, and allow UAM/SMB automation to smoothly cover remaining absorption delayed by GLP-1 therapy.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Zero carb logging causes reactive SMB stacking during late afternoon surges, resulting in severe evening hypoglycemia when meal absorption ends.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrates and bolus timing for 3 consecutive main meals to evaluate whether upfront bolusing prevents afternoon hyperglycemia without causing early post-prandial drops.

exceptions.pattern: Pre-meal glucose below 80 mg/dL or physical activity planned post-meal
exceptions.suggestion: Omit prebolus, deliver 30% immediate bolus at meal start, and log remaining 70% as e-carbs over 2.5-3.0 hours.
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying combined with physical activity or low starting glucose increases early hypoglycemia risk.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Discuss safety updates with your diabetes care team, focusing on overnight target elevation and Max IOB limit reduction.
Step 2: Update the overnight target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL (23:00-08:00) and monitor overnight glucose for 3 nights.
Step 3: Reduce overnight basal (00:00-05:00) from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h and evening basal (18:00-20:00) from 0.6-0.7 U/h to 0.5 U/h.
Step 4: Reduce Max IOB in AAPS settings from 25.0 U to 7.0 U and Max Basal from 12.0 U/h to 4.0 U/h.
Step 5: Begin logging carbohydrate amounts for main meals and testing a 50% upfront pre-bolus strategy.
education: GLP-1 receptor agonists slow stomach emptying, causing carbohydrate absorption to peak hours later than usual.
Unannounced meals force automated systems to guess carb impact, which often leads to late insulin stacking and subsequent hypoglycemia.
Setting a realistic Max IOB guardrail based on Total Daily Dose prevents automated systems from delivering unsafe insulin volumes during sensor errors or delayed meal spikes.
safety_notes: Decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their healthcare provider.
Make parameter changes one at a time and allow at least 3 days of monitoring between adjustments.
Always maintain accessible fast-acting glucose treatments for hypoglycemia management.
